title: Rational 6-cycles of z^2+c
credit: Stoll (2008); open case of the Morton-Silverman / Flynn-Poonen-Schaefer programme
premise_risks: The full statement 'no period > 3' is the named Flynn-Poonen-Schaefer conjecture. This candidate is only its unnamed period-6 case, which the naming rule allows.
An unconditional rank computation for J_1(6) could be within reach of modern class-group methods (as in Fu-Stoll 2024), so difficulty may be lower than it looks.
plain: Iterate the map x ↦ x² + c with c and the starting point x rational. A rational starting point can return to itself after exactly 1, 2 or 3 steps (for example c = −29/16, x = −1/4 gives a 3-cycle), and it is proved that exact periods 4 and 5 are impossible. Show, without assuming unproved conjectures, that exact period 6 is impossible too.
math: Prove that there are no $c,x\in\mathbb{Q}$ such that $x$ has exact (minimal) period $6$ under $f_c(z)=z^2+c$.
